subject: Usage teardown and $/1M token target — confirmation
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Tran <simon.tran@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Usage teardown and $/1M token target — confirmation

Hi Simon — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can get a pricing sketch over to you tomorrow: 

Recap from today's discovery:
- Primary product flow: customer support triage + short-form summarization + in-chat knowledge retrieval (predominantly respond/generate calls).
- Expected active users (initial): 75k MAU, ramping to ~250k over 9 months.
- Average session tokens: 1.8k/session (95th pct 3.5k).
- Concurrency/peaks: baseline concurrent inference ~45 TPS; expected marketing-driven peaks up to 420 TPS for ~30–90 mins/day.

As discussed, the two things we need confirmed to finalize a hosted pricing sketch: 
1) Monthly token estimate (total): please confirm whether the 1) baseline run-rate you mentioned — ~800M tokens/month — is the correct central estimate, and 2) whether to include a 25% buffer for marketing spikes for the pricing model.
2) Target spend and unit economics: you mentioned a target of roughly $7k–$12k/month in initial spend for the POC. Can you confirm a target $/1M tokens (if you track that internally) or the monthly budget band we should aim at?

Next steps from our side if numbers above check out: Marissa will produce a hosted pricing sketch with 3 consumption bands (POC, ramp, enterprise steady-state) and two SLA/throughput options (standard, high-burst). We'll also attach a sample usage CSV so your engineering team can plug in their exact session shapes.

Attachments: I will attach a quick CSV sample and a pricing sketch draft in the next email.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity so we can keep this tight.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwoodinference.com

From: Simon Tran <simon.tran@novacorp.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@novacorp.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage teardown and $/1M token target — confirmation

Thanks Dylan — quick confirmations below: 

- Monthly token estimate: baseline is 800M tokens/month. We want the pricing to show both: (A) conservative baseline (800M) and (B) campaign-adjusted (1.0B) that includes ~25% marketing buffer.
- Peak TPS: engineering confirms 420 TPS peak (observed historically during product launches). These peaks are short — typically 45–90 minutes and occur 2–3x/month.
- Target spend for the POC: our finance sponsor approved a POC budget band of $9k–$15k/month. For the first pass, aim at ~$10k/month target for POC.

One ask: can you show scenarios with and without prefix/KV caching savings? Our embeddings layer will cache recent convo context for frequent customers; we'd like to see the delta.

Simon
Simon Tran
Director, Product — Novacorp
simon.tran@novacorp.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage teardown and $/1M token target — confirmation

Great — that helps a lot, Simon. Two quick clarifications and what we'll deliver by EOD tomorrow: 

Clarifications: 
- We'll include both 800M and 1.0B token scenarios. For the hosted sketch we'll present token-tier pricing and an illustrative $/1M effective cost so you can compare against your budget band.
- For the POC target, we'll produce a configuration that lands ~ $10k/month nominal spend (this will assume a mix of standard model + small proportion quantized variants for cost savings).
- Caching: we'll show a side-by-side: (A) No KV/prefix caching, and (B) Aggressive KV/prefix caching that reflects your embeddings layer behavior. We'll annotate assumptions (cache hit rate, typical prefix length saved).

Deliverables (EOD tomorrow): 
- Pricing sketch PDF (3 bands + caching toggles) — attached file: redwood_pricing_sketch.pdf.
- Sample usage CSV populated from your baseline numbers — attached: novacorp_sample_usage_breakdown.csv.
- Short note on expected peak TPS handling and recommended burst capacity config (we'll recommend a dedicated burst lane for the 420 TPS peaks to preserve latency SLOs).

Marissa — can you include a quick two-row table in the pricing PDF that shows: POC target ($10k/mo) mapped to effective $/1M tokens for both caching on/off? Karthik — can you add a one-paragraph engineering note about the burst-lane configuration we should recommend for Novacorp?

I'll attach the files in the next message.

—Dylan

Subject: Fwd: Pricing sketch + sample usage (Novacorp)

Forwarding the deliverables — attachments included. Quick highlights below so it's easy to scan: 

Attachments (stubs):
- novacorp_sample_usage_breakdown.csv (CSV): columns: month, sessions, avg_tokens_per_session, total_tokens, peak_tps, notes
- redwood_pricing_sketch.pdf (PDF): one-page with three consumption bands and two caching variants; includes an illustrative effective $/1M tokens row.

Highlights: 
- POC band (aimed at $10k/mo): effective $/1M tokens = ~$11.8k for no-caching and ~$8.9k with caching (assumes 30% cache hit on prefixes and 10% reduction from embedding dedupe). Exact numbers are in the PDF.
- Ramp band (800M tokens baseline): effective $/1M tokens = ~$9.5k with caching; ~$13.3k without.
- Peak handling: recommend a burst-lane with autoscale to handle 420 TPS peaks. Estimated incremental cost for burst lane (30–90 min/day) is shown as a delta line item.

Simon — if the POC sketch lands in your band, let's lock a short pilot SOW and schedule a technical kickoff next week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the PDF.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
